source_locator: R2244: Battle of Santa Cruz narrative, sortie of 11 October, and appendix 45 force table; R2243: GeoNames Chuuk Lagoon
notes: USSBS ch. VII: on 11 October the heaviest Japanese naval force assembled since Midway sortied from Truk. This unit is named in the Santa Cruz force table (appendix 45) of that force. Confidence 0.5 (single official family for this departure). Truk lies in the central_pacific box. Filed under OP-TRUK-SORTIE-OCT1942 (central_pacific), not OP-CAMP-GUADALCANAL, so the claim sub_theater matches the operation.

location_qualifier: Shortland Harbour, flagship of the Support Force
source_locator: R2255: C08030768500 PDF p. 1, 11 November 1942, Shortland, flagship Suzuya; R2224: GeoNames Shortland Harbour
notes: JACAR C08030768500 PDF p. 1: Outer South Seas Force Support Force secret operation order no. 1, dated 11 November 1942 at Shortland, flagship Suzuya, commander Nishimura Shoji. The order directs a sortie from the Shortland anchorage that day. Confidence 0.5 (one official family). Shortland Harbour is a gazetteer harbour point already in the dataset (R2224). The operation_id on this row was OP-NAVAL-GUADALCANAL. It is now OP-CAMP-GUADALCANAL, because 11 November is a Shortland sortie and approach day, one day before the Naval Battle of Guadalcanal (12–15 November), and naval sortie, approach and withdrawal claims outside a battle's date window are tagged to the parent campaign.
